title: SRD: a space holding a creature that isn't Tiny or your ally is Difficult Terrain; engine: moving through a hostile creature's space costs 1 ft per foot

history.summary:
T-100 is fixed. When a creature moves, every 5-ft square it enters that overlaps the space of another creature now costs 1 extra foot, unless that creature is Tiny, an ally (game.is_ally), dead, being dragged by the mover, or at a different elevation. This change is in `combat.move`, in the new helper `_feet_in_crowded_spaces`. It uses two new geometry helpers: `steps_between` lists the squares a move enters, and `squares_overlap` checks whether two squares share any interior.

The extra cost isn't stacked (clause #3). If the whole move is already charged as Difficult Terrain, whether from the scene's terrain, a `difficult=True` move, or the extra cost of swimming or climbing without the Speed, the creature's space adds nothing on top.

When extra feet are charged, a `difficult-terrain` event is logged after the movement is spent, so a refused move logs nothing. It cites page 181 and GLOSS.difficult-terrain#5, and adds ruling R-43 when one of the creatures isn't hostile.

Checks run:
- The ticket's test passes with `--runxfail`.
- The unit tests pass (563).
- `ruff check` and `ruff format --check` are clean.
- `dev-gate` passes.
- In the full suite, the only failures are strict XPASSes for T-100 to T-104 (T-101 move command, T-102 indifferent bystander, T-103 Small creature, T-104 a move that costs more than Speed is refused); this fix closes those other four tickets too.
- T-99 (the Web area) still xfails as expected.
